newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Dec 18.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.

-- An upcoming expiry of the mandates of two Bank of France Monetary Policy Council members may allow French President Jacques Chirac to modify its political balance. Supporters of monetary orthodoxy and a strong franc oppose possible entry of an anti-Maastricht member to the independent Council.

-- Government to put up for sale a 58.63 percent stake held by Thomson in defence unit Thomson-CSF. Analysts estimate the value of Thomson-CSF around 24 billion francs, higher than its current 20-billion-franc bourse value, raising the question of whether potential bidders have enough cash to buy it. Lagardere unit Matra is seen by analysts as a favourite candidate.
-- Employers and unions in transport sector start six month talks on working hours.

-- Members of Parliament agree conditionally to a planned merger between nuclear plant manufacturer Framatome and GEC-Alsthom. Conditions include Parliamentary control over the French nuclear industry, an extension until 2001 of a cooperation between Framatome and Cogema, and a strategic veto for the state shareholder.
